# Exact coefficient formulation and calibration for low-maximum simplex normals

This note proves the reformulation and limiting family below. It does
not prove a universal 4/9 lower bound.

Let d>=2, u_i>=0, sum_i u_i=1, and max_i u_i<=2/(d+1). For X
uniform on T_d=conv(0,e_1,...,e_d), the cap through its centroid is

    P(u.X>=1/(d+1)).                                    (1)

Take independent standard exponential variables E_0,...,E_d and put
S=sum_i E_i. The vector (E_0/S,...,E_d/S) is uniform in barycentric
coordinates of T_d, by the elementary change of variables from the
independent exponential density to total S and barycentric coordinates.
Set

    a_0=-1,       a_i=(d+1)u_i-1 for i>=1.

Then (1) equals

    P(sum_(i=0)^d a_i E_i>=0),                          (2)

where a_i in [-1,1], a_0=-1, and sum_i a_i=0. Conversely, every such
finite coefficient vector comes from a permitted positive normal by
u_i=(1+a_i)/(d+1). Thus the coefficient structure, including the fixed
coefficient -1, is exact.

Writing Z=sum_(i=1)^d a_i E_i and conditioning on Z gives

    (1)=E[(1-exp(-Z))_+],       E Z=1.                  (3)

The law in (3) remains the specified sum of signed independent
exponentials. Replacing it by an arbitrary law of mean one is not a
valid relaxation for a proposed improved lower bound.

## A rigorous concentrated-coefficient calibration

Fix an integer k>=1 and let N tend to infinity. Choose the coefficients

    a_0=-1,
    k further coefficients equal to +1,
    N further coefficients equal to -(k-1)/N.

For N>=k-1 all coefficients belong to [-1,1] and their sum is zero,
so they define actual low-maximum simplex normals in dimension d=k+N.
The sum of the last N exponential terms has mean k-1 and variance
(k-1)^2/N, so it converges in probability to k-1. Independence and the
continuous distribution of the remaining terms then give the exact
limiting cap probability

    I_k=P(Gamma(k,1)>=k-1+Exp(1)).                       (4)

The two variables in (4) are independent. Integrating the integer-gamma
tail against the exponential density gives

    I_k=exp(-(k-1))
         *sum_(j=0)^(k-1) [(k-1)^j/j!]*(1-2^(-(k-j))). (5)

In particular I_1=1/2, I_2=5/(4e), I_3=27/(8e^2), and
I_4=147/(16e^3). Thus a universal half-mass bound is impossible even
in a smooth high-dimensional limiting family, independently of the
finite d=4 counterexample in
`candidate f670e4af83fa9465`.

Formula (5) is a calibration family, not an extremal characterization.
No claim is made that concentrating positive coefficients or spreading
negative coefficients minimizes (2).

## Exact falsification search, explicitly not a proof

The script `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/search_low_maximum_centroid_cap_exact_minkowski.py` computes
cap fractions as rational confluent divided differences of the positive
dth power on the centered projection knots. It tested 4,374 actual
coefficient vectors: rational bounded-coefficient samples in dimensions
2 through 25, and the preceding concentrated family through dimension
120. Every comparison with 4/9 was exact. It found no counterexample.
The smallest value in the concentrated test family was approximately
0.4576216434 at d=120,k=3; its exact rational fraction and all sampled
minima are retained in
`../assets/pk-nov6/computations/low_maximum_centroid_cap_exact_search_minkowski.json`.

This finite calculation supplies no proof of the proposed 4/9 bound,
no concentration principle, and no result for all low-maximum normals.
